2027-04-22.title: Fourth Thursday of Resurrection
2027-04-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Honour with the lips, and the heart far away
2027-04-22.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). A day to examine the heart: the readings speak of teachers who deny the Lord who bought them, and of worship that stays on the lips.
2027-04-22.verse: This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me;
theo: The Second Letter of Peter was written for Christians who had received the faith from the apostles and were now hearing other voices. Peter does not pretend the Church will be spared trouble from within: “But false prophets also arose among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you, who will secretly bring in destructive opinions. They will even deny the Master who bought them—bringing swift destruction on themselves.” Two things mark these false teachers. They work secretly, slipping their opinions in beside the true faith so that the change is hardly noticed. And they deny the Master who bought them. The word is the language of the slave market: Christ has paid the price for us, with his own Blood, and we belong to him. A teaching that empties the Cross, or reduces the Resurrection to a pleasant idea, or makes Jesus one teacher among many, denies the very Lord who bought us. Peter adds a sad note: “many will follow their licentious ways, and because of these teachers the way of truth will be maligned.” False doctrine and loose living travel together, and when Christians live badly, the world speaks ill of the faith itself. Finally, “in their greed they will exploit you with deceptive words.” Then as now, some made religion a business.

How do we recognise a false teacher? The Church has never answered by asking each Christian to judge alone. The same letter reminds its readers to remember “the commandment of the Lord and Savior spoken through your apostles” (2 Peter 3:2). The test is the faith of the apostles, handed down in the Scriptures, kept in the living Tradition and taught by the bishops in communion with the successor of Peter. Our own Church carries this memory deeply. For centuries the Thomas Christians of Kerala lived the faith received from the apostle with very few books; when strangers came with new teachings, the people asked one question: is this what our fathers received? The Easter season is a good time to hold fast to the apostolic faith, because it rests on the apostles' witness to the Risen Lord. They did not hand on an opinion. They handed on what they had seen and heard and touched. A sound test for any new voice, on a screen or in a meeting, is this: does it lead me to Christ crucified and risen, to the sacraments and to love of the Church, or away from them?

In the Gospel some Pharisees and scribes come from Jerusalem and ask why the disciples do not wash their hands before eating, as the tradition of the elders required. The washing was a religious rite, not a matter of hygiene, and many devout people kept it with love. Jesus does not attack washing; he exposes a misuse. Some had found a way to declare their savings dedicated to God, Korban, so that they need not support their aged parents: “So, for the sake of your tradition, you make void the word of God.” And he quotes Isaiah: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me; in vain do they worship me, teaching human precepts as doctrines.” This is a word for religious people of every age, and first for us. Jesus is not speaking against the Jewish people, nor against tradition as such; he himself kept the feasts and prayed in the synagogue, and the Church lives by the apostolic Tradition. He is speaking against any custom, ours included, that becomes a way to avoid love. A Syro-Malabar Christian may keep every fast, every feast and every family custom, and still neglect an old father or speak bitterly of a neighbour. Then our worship is lip-service. Easter asks for a new heart: the Risen Lord does not want only our lips at the Qurbana, but hearts that go home and honour father and mother.
conn: “Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you; they are deluding you” (Jeremiah 23:16); Jesus warns, “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing” (Matthew 7:15).
“For you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body” (1 Corinthians 6:20); “you were ransomed… with the precious blood of Christ” (1 Peter 1:18–19).
“Stand firm and hold fast to the traditions that you were taught by us, either by word of mouth or by our letter” (2 Thessalonians 2:15).
The fourth commandment (Exodus 20:12), “the first commandment with a promise” (Ephesians 6:2).
Jesus quotes Isaiah 29:13; Paul writes, “one believes with the heart and so is justified, and one confesses with the mouth and so is saved” (Romans 10:10).
“A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you” (Ezekiel 36:26).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Church prays the words handed down from the apostles: this is the Tradition that leads us to the Lord who bought us with his Blood, present on the altar.
Before we come to Communion we are invited to make peace and to purify the heart; the Lord wants lips that confess him and hearts that are near him.
outline: A young Church hearing new voices.
Point 1 · They will deny the Master who bought them
Point 2 · Hold fast to the apostolic faith
The test of what our fathers received.
Customs that serve love, and customs that avoid it.
A son who stops making excuses and goes to sit with his old father on the veranda.
“This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.”
live: Before you share a religious video or message, ask: does it lead to Christ, the sacraments and the Church?
Look at a crucifix today and say: Lord, you bought me; I am yours.
Do one concrete thing this week for your parents or an elderly relative: a visit, a call, a task done.
At the Qurbana this week, choose one prayer and mean every word of it.
fathers: The tradition of the apostles, made known throughout the whole world, can be found in every Church by those who wish to see the truth. We can name those whom the apostles appointed bishops and their successors down to our own time; they taught nothing like the fantasies of the heretics. The truth is easy to find, for the apostles deposited it in the Church as in a rich treasury.

Sing to God not only with the voice but with the heart. Many have the voice and are silent within; others are silent and their heart cries to God. Let your life sing: when the voice is quiet, let your love be heard.
magis: The apostles entrusted the Gospel to their successors, the bishops; Sacred Tradition and Sacred Scripture are bound together, flowing from the same divine wellspring; ecclesial traditions are distinct from the apostolic Tradition and can be retained, modified or abandoned.
The task of authentically interpreting the word of God has been entrusted to the living teaching office of the Church, which serves the word of God and is not above it.
The fourth commandment: grown children have duties toward their parents; they must give them material and moral support in old age and in sickness.
Outward sacrifice, to be genuine, must be the expression of spiritual sacrifice: a broken and contrite heart.
The Jews are not collectively responsible for the death of Jesus; Jesus' disputes with some Pharisees do not justify blame on the Jewish people.
saints: 19–25 April: fourth week of the Resurrection. Wed 21: in the Latin calendar, St Anselm. Fri 23: in the Latin calendar, St George. Sat 24: in the Syro-Malabar calendar, St George, Martyr (Geevarghese Sahada), an important feast. Sun 25: Fifth Sunday of Resurrection, with Mar Addai; St Mark the Evangelist (25 Apr) gives way to the Sunday this year (verify locally).
2027-04-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you bought us with your precious Blood, and you want our hearts, not only our lips. Keep us faithful to the faith of the apostles, handed down in your Church, and guard us from voices that would lead us away from you. Deliver us from customs that excuse us from love. Give us new hearts that honour our parents, care for the elderly and worship you in spirit and truth. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

2027-04-22.action: Do one concrete act of care for your parents or an elderly relative today.
2027-04-22.question: Is there a custom in my life that has become a way to avoid love?
kidsaint: Thomas was one of the twelve apostles. When he saw the Risen Jesus he said, “My Lord and my God!” The Christians of Kerala believe he came to India and taught our ancestors about Jesus. For hundreds of years they kept his faith carefully and handed it to their children. Lesson: the faith you learn at home is a treasure passed down from the apostles!
term: A Hebrew word meaning ‘offering’ or ‘gift dedicated to God’. Mark's Gospel uses it in the parallel passage (Mark 7:11). Jesus criticises the misuse of such a vow to avoid supporting one's parents: no religious practice can cancel the commandment of love.

family.explain: Some people asked Jesus why his friends did not wash their hands in a special religious way before eating. Jesus said that some people used religious rules to avoid looking after their own mother and father! He said: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” That means saying nice prayers is good, but God also wants us to really love, especially at home.
family.intention: We pray for grandparents and all old people, especially those who are lonely.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week to make Ammachi and Appachan, or an old neighbour, happy?”

illus: A man in Changanassery was known in his parish as a pillar of the church: he never missed the Sunday Qurbana, led the prayer group and organised the feast. His old father lived alone in the ancestral house a few kilometres away, and the son visited him only at Christmas and Easter. One Lent the vicar spoke about the Gospel of today, and the man went home uneasy. The next evening he drove to his father's house and found him sitting alone on the veranda in the dark. He sat beside him and they said the rosary together. After that he went every Thursday. He said later, “I had been honouring God with my lips. My father taught me where my heart had been missing.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you bought us with your Blood. Draw our hearts near to you now, so that our prayer may be more than words. Amen. Alleluia!
share: They will even deny the Master who bought them (2 Peter 2:1). What voices in my life lead me away from Christ?
Because of these teachers the way of truth will be maligned (2 Peter 2:2). Does my way of life make the faith attractive or not?
For the sake of your tradition, you make void the word of God (Matthew 15:6). Have I used any custom to avoid a duty of love?
This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Matthew 15:8). How can my heart be nearer to God in prayer?
pm.resp: Lord, draw our hearts near to you.
interc: For the Church, that she may remain faithful to the faith of the apostles and teach it with love.
For those who have been led astray by false teachings, that they may find their way back to Christ.
For elderly parents who are neglected or lonely, that their children may honour and care for them.
For all who use religion for gain, that they may repent.
For ourselves, that our worship may come from the heart.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to buy us back with his Blood, and you call us to worship you in spirit and truth. Keep us in the faith of the apostles, and give us hearts that love you and honour those you have given us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, today Peter warns us about false teachers, and Jesus warns us about worship that stays on the lips.

Peter says false teachers will come, bringing in destructive opinions secretly, and “They will even deny the Master who bought them.” Christ bought us with his own Blood. A teaching that empties the Cross or the Resurrection denies the very Lord who bought us.

How do we know true teaching? The Church answers: by the faith of the apostles, handed down in Scripture and Tradition and taught by the bishops in communion with Peter's successor. Our forefathers in Kerala kept the faith of St Thomas for centuries by asking: is this what our fathers received?

In the Gospel Jesus sees some who used a religious vow to avoid supporting their parents. He says: “for the sake of your tradition, you make void the word of God.” And he quotes Isaiah: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.”
This word is for us first. We can keep every fast and feast and still neglect our parents or speak bitterly of a neighbour. Jesus wants our hearts, not only our lips.
So today, let us test the voices we listen to, look at the crucifix and remember the price, and do one real act of love for our parents. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said some people said nice prayers with their mouths, but their hearts were far from God. God wants our hearts too!
Today, show love at home with your hands and your heart: help Amma or Appa without being asked!

intro: Theme: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.”
False teachers who deny the Master who bought them, the apostolic faith as our test, and worship that reaches the heart.

points.h: They will deny the Master who bought them
q: Thus says the LORD of hosts: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you; they are deluding you. They speak visions of their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.

But false prophets also arose among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you, who will secretly bring in destructive opinions. They will even deny the Master who bought them—bringing swift destruction on themselves.
points.apply: Before you share a religious message, ask whether it leads to Christ and his Church.

points.h: Hold fast to the apostolic faith
sub: The commandment spoken through the apostles.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
So then, brothers and sisters, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions that you were taught by us, either by word of mouth or by our letter.
points.apply: Teach or review one article of the Creed at home this week.

sub: Not against tradition, but against avoiding love.
A new heart that honours father and mother.
q: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their worship of me is a human commandment learned by rote;
For one believes with the heart and so is justified, and one confesses with the mouth and so is saved.
points.apply: Do one concrete act of care for your parents or an elderly relative today.

concl: The Lord who bought us with his Blood wants our faith whole and our hearts near.
Let us hold to what the apostles handed down and let our love begin at home.
2027-04-22.resolve: This week, test the voices you follow, remember the price of your redemption before a crucifix, and honour your parents with a deed of love.
